findings.title: Observing one project deletes other projects’ polling state
findings.description: `RunnerTenant` shares one observer across all projects, but these lines retain only the current project’s entries. Ticking another project—even an empty one—erases polling timestamps, overdue markers, and cached faults. Reproduced A → empty B → A polling A twice at the same clock time despite the configured interval. Scope observer state and cleanup per project, and add a multi-project regression test.

findings.title: Launch can start after the deadline or a stop request
findings.description: The budget check happens before journaling, but the database commit and log creation precede `Popen` without another check. If that work crosses the deadline or receives a stop request, the child still launches. Reproduced a journal operation advancing beyond the deadline and requesting stop: launch proceeded and `_act` returned `COMPLETE`. Recheck immediately before spawning and explicitly reconcile any journaled-but-unlaunched entry.

findings.title: Unconfirmed launches lose standing poll faults between polls
findings.description: After an unconfirmed launch receives `PollFailure`, subsequent ticks inside the polling interval call `_still_overdue` without replaying `_faulted`. Reproduced the state changing from `FAULT` to `LAUNCHING` with no reported fault one second later, although no successful poll occurred. Consequently, `_close_recovered` can close the escalation prematurely. Replay standing faults until a usable observation supersedes them.

findings.title: Repeated unexpected faults bypass the idle interval
findings.description: The exception handler always reports a write, even when `escalate` deduplicates an existing escalation or finds an already-blocked node. `ResidentProcess._loop` waits only when tenants report no work, so a persistent exception produces a tight retry-and-error-log loop. Have escalation report whether it actually changed the store, and combine that with `tick.wrote` instead of returning unconditional `True`.
